gotchas: Your mixin target is CORRECT as written. useItemOn(LocalPlayer, InteractionHand, BlockHitResult) is verbatim what javap prints, so `@Inject(method = "useItemOn", ...)` resolves. But note the asymmetry: useItemOn takes LocalPlayer while useItem takes Player — the mixin already handles this (it fully-qualifies LocalPlayer on the useItemOn handler and uses Player on the useItem handler). Do not 'tidy' them to the same type.

useItemOn OWNS the sequence number — a caller must not supply one. It calls startPrediction(minecraft.level, sequence -> { result.setValue(performUseItemOn(...)); return new ServerboundUseItemOnPacket(hand, blockHit, sequence); }). startPrediction pulls the int from BlockStatePredictionHandler.currentSequence(), passes it into the lambda, sends the returned packet, and closes the handler. Ack comes back as ClientboundBlockChangedAckPacket(int) -> ClientPacketListener.handleBlockChangedAck -> endPredictionsUpTo. Calling useItemOn is sufficient for a correctly ack-tracked interaction.

You cannot legally hand-roll the prediction from a mod package: ClientLevel.getBlockStatePredictionHandler() is PACKAGE-PRIVATE on 26.2 (javap prints no access modifier). Sending your own ServerboundUseItemOnPacket with a made-up sequence, or with sequence 0, desyncs the prediction handler and causes ghost blocks. Go through useItemOn.

Ordering inside useItemOn: performUseItemOn (the client-side world mutation / itemStack.useOn) runs INSIDE the lambda, therefore BEFORE connection.send(). An @Inject at HEAD of performUseItemOn is already inside the prediction scope; a HEAD inject on useItemOn is outside it, which is why cancelling there and returning FAIL is safe (no sequence gets burned).

useItemOn DOES NOT SWING. Neither does performUseItemOn. The swing lives in the private Minecraft.startUseItem(), and it is CONDITIONAL: `if (useResult instanceof Success success) { if (success.swingSource() == SwingSource.CLIENT) { this.player.swing(hand); ... } return; }`. Unconditionally calling player.swing() after useItemOn double-swings whenever swingSource() == SERVER, because ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleUseItemOn itself does `this.player.swing(hand, true)` in that case.

InteractionResult is an INTERFACE on 26.2, not an enum, and CONSUME is an InteractionResult$Success instance. So `result instanceof InteractionResult.Success` is TRUE for CONSUME as well as SUCCESS/SUCCESS_SERVER. Do not use == comparisons against InteractionResult.SUCCESS to mean 'it worked'; use consumesAction(), and use swingSource() to decide about the arm. Any pre-26.x code doing `if (result == InteractionResult.SUCCESS)` or expecting InteractionResultHolder is broken.

useItemOn does NO client-side reach check. Its only pre-send guard is the world border: `if (!this.minecraft.level.getWorldBorder().isWithinBounds(blockHit.getBlockPos())) return InteractionResult.FAIL;` — it returns InteractionResult.FAIL on that failure. Other early exits, all inside performUseItemOn: spectator -> InteractionResult.CONSUME; block whose requiredFeatures are not enabled -> FAIL; empty stack or item on cooldown -> PASS. This means you can call useItemOn with an arbitrarily distant BlockHitResult and the client will happily simulate and send it.

Vanilla's reach limit is enforced upstream, not in useItemOn: Minecraft.pick(float) -> LocalPlayer.raycastHitResult(float, Entity), whose private filterHitResult() rewrites any hit farther than blockInteractionRange()/entityInteractionRange() into BlockHitResult.miss(...). For entities Minecraft.startUseItem additionally checks player.isWithinEntityInteractionRange(entity, 0.0) explicitly; there is NO corresponding explicit block-range check in startUseItem. If you synthesize your own BlockHitResult you have bypassed the entire range system client-side.

The server still checks. ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleUseItemOn (server-only, ServerPlayer/ServerLevel, uncallable from client) requires player.isWithinBlockInteractionRange(pos, 1.0) — failing that it silently drops the packet with no feedback — and requires each axis of (hitLocation - blockCentre) to be < 1.0000001 or it logs 'Rejecting UseItemOnPacket from {}: Location {} too far away from hit block {}'. Mirror it client-side with the public Player.isWithinBlockInteractionRange(BlockPos, double) before sending.

handleInventoryMouseClick and net.minecraft.world.inventory.ClickType are both GONE on 26.2. Use handleContainerInput(int containerId, int slotNum, int buttonNum, ContainerInput containerInput, Player player) and net.minecraft.world.inventory.ContainerInput (in minecraft-common, so it is available to non-client code too). 'Swap with hotbar slot N' is ContainerInput.SWAP with buttonNum = N in 0..8; buttonNum = 40 means the offhand. Verified in AbstractContainerMenu.doClick's guard `containerInput == ContainerInput.SWAP && (buttonNum >= 0 && buttonNum < 9 || buttonNum == 40)`, which then reads `inventory.getItem(buttonNum)`.

handleContainerInput silently no-ops (LOGGER.warn 'Ignoring click in mismatching container') when the containerId you pass does not equal player.containerMenu.containerId. Always read the id off the live menu: player.containerMenu.containerId. It also snapshots every slot before calling menu.clicked(...) and ships only the changed slots as HashedStack — so mutating the menu yourself before calling it corrupts the diff the server receives.

MultiPlayerGameMode contains NO right-click rate limiter. Its gating fields are all block-BREAKING state: destroyDelay (private int, set to 5, consumed at the top of continueDestroyBlock), isDestroying (private boolean, public getter isDestroying()), destroyProgress (private float), destroyTicks (private float), destroyBlockPos (private BlockPos), destroyingItem (private ItemStack), carriedIndex (private int). The right-click throttle is Minecraft.rightClickDelay (PRIVATE int, set to 4 in startUseItem, decremented once per Minecraft.tick()), and it only gates the held-key auto-repeat branch. Calling gameMode.useItemOn directly is completely unthrottled — implement your own delay or you will spam N packets per tick.

Minecraft.startUseItem() is PRIVATE, so you cannot reuse vanilla's full right-click path (hand loop over InteractionHand.values(), isHandsBusy/isDestroying gates, feature-flag check, swing decision, itemInHandRenderer.itemUsed) without an accessor mixin. If you call useItemOn directly you must replicate whichever of those you need. Two easy-to-miss ones: startUseItem returns early on `useResult instanceof Fail` (it does NOT fall through to useItem for that hand), and it only calls gameRenderer.itemInHandRenderer.itemUsed(hand) when the stack count actually changed or the player hasInfiniteMaterials().

MultiPlayerGameMode has no reach accessor at all — do not look for getPickRange/getReach here. Use Player.blockInteractionRange() / Player.entityInteractionRange() (both public doubles, inherited by LocalPlayer), the predicates isWithinBlockInteractionRange(BlockPos, double) / isWithinEntityInteractionRange(Entity, double), and the constants Player.DEFAULT_BLOCK_INTERACTION_RANGE = 4.5f / DEFAULT_ENTITY_INTERACTION_RANGE = 3.0f. Both values are attribute-driven (Attributes.BLOCK_INTERACTION_RANGE / ENTITY_INTERACTION_RANGE), so never hardcode 4.5/3.0 — read the accessor.

Hotbar sync is automatic and you almost never need to touch it. ensureHasSentCarriedItem() is PRIVATE and runs (a) as the first statement of MultiPlayerGameMode.tick(), which Minecraft.tick() invokes in its 'gameMode' profiler section — BEFORE this.pick(1.0F), before gui.tick(), and before handleKeybinds() reaches startUseItem/useItemOn — and (b) as the first statement of useItemOn itself, plus useItem, continueDestroyBlock, attack, interact, releaseUsingItem, piercingAttack. So switching slots and calling useItemOn in the same tick still emits ServerboundSetCarriedItemPacket ahead of ServerboundUseItemOnPacket. It is NOT called by startDestroyBlock or destroyBlock.

But ensureHasSentCarriedItem() only fires when minecraft.player.getInventory().getSelectedSlot() != carriedIndex. Switch slots via Inventory.setSelectedSlot(int) (26.2 name — not a `selected` field). If you send your own ServerboundSetCarriedItemPacket without changing the inventory field, carriedIndex goes stale and a later genuine slot change can be skipped, leaving the server holding the wrong item during your interaction.

26.2 added rotation to the item-use packet: useItem builds `new ServerboundUseItemPacket(hand, sequence, player.getYRot(), player.getXRot())` and reads the rotations at send time inside the prediction lambda. A module that spoofs rotation must have the yaw/pitch already applied to the player before calling useItem, or the server sees the real rotation. useItemOn's packet carries no rotation — only hand, blockHit, sequence.

MultiPlayerGameMode.interact (entity right-click) does NOT use startPrediction — it sends ServerboundInteractPacket directly with no sequence number. Do not assume every entry point on this class is prediction-wrapped; only useItemOn, useItem, startDestroyBlock and continueDestroyBlock are.

MultiPlayerGameMode lives in minecraft-client-only.jar (verified: 0 hits in minecraft-common.jar, 1 in minecraft-client-only.jar), so anything referencing it must stay in the client source set. ContainerInput and Player, by contrast, are in minecraft-common.
